pairs: Voca ergo,
Therefore call,
si est qui tibi respondeat,
if there are any who will respond to you,
et ad aliquem sanctorum convertere.
and turn to one or another of the saints.
Vere stultum interficit iracundia,
Truly, anger condemns the foolish to death,
et parvulum occidit invidia.
and envy kills the petty.
Ego vidi stultum firma radice,
I have seen a fool with a strong root,
et maledixi pulchritudini ejus statim.
and I have cursed his excellence without hesitation.
Longe fient filii ejus a salute,
His sons will be far from prosperity
et conterentur in porta,
and will be crushed at the gate,
et non erit qui eruat.
and there will be none who can rescue them.
Cujus messem famelicus comedet,
Their harvest, the starving will eat.
et ipsum rapiet armatus,
The armed man will rob him,
et bibent sitientes divitias ejus.
and the thirsty will drink his resources.
Nihil in terra sine causa fit,
Nothing on earth occurs without a reason,
et de humo non oritur dolor.
and sorrow does not rise from the earth.
Homo nascitur ad laborem,
Man is born to labor,
et avis ad volatum.
and the bird to fly.
Quam ob rem ego deprecabor Dominum,
Therefore, because of this, I will beg the Lord,
et ad Deum ponam eloquium meum:
and place my eloquence before God.
qui facit magna et inscrutabilia, et mirabilia absque numero;
He does great and unfathomable and miraculous things without number.
qui dat pluviam super faciem terræ,
He gives rain over the face of the earth
et irrigat aquis universa;
and irrigates all things with the waters.
qui ponit humiles in sublime,
He places the humble on high
et mœrentes erigit sospitate;
and encourages the grieving towards health.
qui dissipat cogitationes malignorum,
He dispels the thoughts of the spiteful,
ne possint implere manus eorum quod cœperant;
lest their hands be able to complete what they had begun.
qui apprehendit sapientes in astutia eorum,
He catches the wise in their cleverness
et consilium pravorum dissipat.
and dissipates the counsel of the perverse.
Per diem incurrent tenebras,
They will encounter darkness in the daytime,
et quasi in nocte, sic palpabunt in meridie.
and they will grope at midday just as in the night.
Porro salvum faciet egenum a gladio oris eorum,
Thereafter, he will act to save the needy from the sword of their mouth,
et de manu violenti pauperem.
and the poor from the hand of the violent.
Et erit egeno spes;
And there will be hope for those in need,
iniquitas autem contrahet os suum.
for iniquity will diminish its speech.
Beatus homo qui corripitur a Deo:
Blessed is the man whom God corrects;
increpationem ergo Domini ne reprobes:
therefore, do not reject the chastisement of the Lord.
quia ipse vulnerat,
For he wounds
et medetur;
and he cures;
percutit,
he strikes
et manus ejus sanabunt.
and his hands will heal.
In sex tribulationibus liberabit te,
He will deliver you into six tribulations,
et in septima non tanget te malum.
and in the seventh, evil will not touch you.
In fame eruet te de morte,
During famine, he will rescue you from death,
et in bello de manu gladii.
and during war, from the hand of the sword.
A flagello linguæ absconderis,
You will be hidden from the scourge of the tongue,
et non timebis calamitatem cum venerit.
and you will not fear calamity when it arrives.
In vastitate
In desolation and in famine,
et fame ridebis,
you will laugh,
et bestias terræ non formidabis.
and you will not dread the beasts of the earth.
Sed cum lapidibus regionum pactum tuum,
For you are in harmony with the stones of the land,
et bestiæ terræ pacificæ erunt tibi.
and the beasts of the earth will make peace with you.
Et scies quod pacem habeat tabernaculum tuum;
And you will know that your home has peace, and,
et visitans speciem tuam,
concerning your appearance,
non peccabis.
you will not sin.
Scies quoque quoniam multiplex erit semen tuum,
Likewise,
et progenies tua quasi herba terræ.
you will know that your offspring will be manifold and your progeny will be like the grass of the earth.
Ingredieris in abundantia sepulchrum,
You will enter the grave with abundance,
sicut infertur acervus tritici in tempore suo.
just as a crop of wheat is gathered in its time.
Ecce hoc, ut investigavimus,
Behold, this is just as we have found it,
ita est: quod auditum,
which you have heard;
mente pertracta.
walk it through your mind.
